messages:
maria: Quick check-in — ran 50 replay seeds vs our synthetic zipf generator across the kv-prefix bench. Results look ... messy. Hit-rate variance across seeds is 4.8%–13.2% (not a typo).
kevin: Oof. 50 seeds? are those independent replay traces or resampled from the same trace with different start offsets?
maria: Independent replay seeds: we randomize request ordering and start offset, but keep client arrival times the same. Synth generator used zipf alpha=1.1 with the same global QPS.
lisa: Can you paste the exact configs? might be a skewness mismatch between replay and synth.
maria: Sure — snippet: 
```
replay.conf: { seed: $SEED, warmup_seconds: 60, arrival_profile: fixed_qps }
synth.conf: { generator: zipf, alpha: 1.1, warmup_seconds: 60, clients: 16 }
```
andre: Interesting that warmup_seconds is the same — but replay preserves temporal locality (bursts) that synth doesn't. That explains higher hit-rate variance.
kevin: Any correlation between seed and kernel selection logs? e.g., different seeds trigger different mini-batch sizes or kernel paths?
maria: Yes — and this is the key wrinkle. When hot prefixes concentrate, we hit a different kernel (smaller sequence path) which keeps KV lookups localized and increases hit-rate. When spread, kernel picks a path that evicts more aggressively. Profiling sample: 
```
hotspots: kv_cache_lookup: 38%, kernel_select: 22%, batch_assemble: 14%
seed=17: kv_hit=0.792
seed=32: kv_hit=0.655
```
andre: Also saw an intermittent correctness flake under concurrent eviction + kernel-swap. Repro: run `./bench --replay --seed 27 --concurrency 48` and you'll sometimes get stale hits (race on entry->version). Filing a micro test.
lisa: That's a regression candidate for the kernel swap refactor. Did you capture call stacks?
andre: Yep — adding to the ticket with gcore + perf output. Seems like eviction marks then kernel swap reorders the lookup completion path.
ci-bot: smoke/kv-prefix (seed=27) — failure: kv_consistency_check (flaky) — see https://ci/reports/1948765 for logs
kevin: For apples-to-apples we should: 1) fix warmup determinism (seeded warmup traces), 2) sweep zipf alpha (0.8–1.4) with same burstiness, 3) run N seeds and report median + IQR, not mean.
maria: Agreed. Also propose adding a small 'burstiness' param to synth generator that replays Poisson clusters so we can match replay autocorrelation.
lisa: Can we add a kernel-aware metric: %requests routed to small-seq kernel vs long-seq? That'll help explain hit-rate deltas.
maria: Good idea — I already surfaced kernel_select in the profiler but add it to per-run summary.
andre: I'm triaging the race now. If it's real we'll pin a quick fix (atomic eviction state) and rerun the seed sweep.
kevin: Plan: Hold patch window until we confirm whether regression is from kernel-swap or just traffic skew. Run full sweep on dedicated perf pool Monday.
maria: I'll start running a 100-seed batch on the perf pool with the new synth burstiness param and post aggregates. Thanks y'all. :thumbsup:
kevin: Thanks — and please include raw per-seed CSV so we can visualize long tails.
maria: Will do. attaching current CSVs to the ticket in ~30m.
